title: At the Doctor's / N'ụlọ ọgwụ
bridge: Na Spanish, tụkwasịrị na ị ga-eme ka ndị mmadụ na-akpọ 'me duele' tụọnụ na ndị ahu (me duele la cabeza). Na English, nke a dị mkpa ma ọ bụrụ na ọnọdụ ndoro ndoro adịghị ike: 'I have' + 'a headache' (ana m enweta a headache). Ọ bụ ọtụtụ ike ihe mere ka ndị ahu na-akpọ 'I hurt my head' na ụdị ogologo. N'ihi ya, na English, 'hurt' na-eme ka ọ bụ verb: 'My head hurts' (isi m na-eme). Ihe mere ka ị nwere ike ịmụta ihe ndoro ndoro na-akpọ 'have' tụọnụ na nouns ndoro ndoro na 'hurt' tụọnụ na subjects.
rule: Iji kwuo na ndị mmadụ na-eme ihe ndoro ndoro na English na level A2, anyị na-eme ka ndị ahu na-akpọ: 1) 'I have' + noun (a headache, a cold, a fever, a cough, a sore throat, a stomachache, etc.) tụọnụ na ị na-eme na ị nwere ihe. 2) 'My [ndị ahu]' + 'hurts' ma ọ bụ 'My [ndị ahu] is sore' tụọnụ na ị na-eme na ndị ahu na-eme. 3) 'I feel' + adjective (sick, dizzy, tired, etc.) tụọnụ na ndị ahu na-eme na ụdị ndoro ndoro. Na ndoro ndoro na ndoro ndoro, anyị na-eme ka ndị ahu na-akpọ 'do/does' (Do you have...? Yes, I do. No, I don't). Na ihe ndoro ndoro, anyị na-eme ka ndị ahu na-akpọ 'should' / 'shouldn't' (You should rest, You shouldn't eat spicy food). Cheta na 'hurt' bụ verb irregular: hurt - hurt - hurt. Ọ bụghị ihe mere ka 'me duele' na-akpọ nke na-adịghị ike; ọ na-akpọ nke ahu: 'My head hurts' (ị bụghị 'I hurt my head' tụọnụ na ọ bụ na ọ bụ accident). N'ihi ya, ọ bụghị ihe mere ka 'I've got' tụọnụ na 'I have got' (I've got a cold). Na ndoro ndoro ndoro, anyị na-eme ka ndị ahu na-akpọ 'I have a cold'.

concept_examples.text: I have a headache and a sore throat.
concept_examples.translation: Ana m enweta isi na ọnụ na-eme.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ hæv ə ˈhɛdeɪk ənd ə sɔːr θroʊt/

concept_examples.translation: Isi m na-eme ugwo ugwo ugwo ugwo ugwo ugwo ugwo ugwo ugwo ugwo ugwo.

concept_examples.text: You should drink a lot of water.
concept_examples.translation: Ị ga-eme ka ị nwere ike inye mmiri nke dị mma.
concept_examples.phonetic: /juː ʃʊd drɪŋk ə lɒt əv ˈwɔːtər/

common_error.explanation: Ọ bụ ihe mere ka ndị ahu na-akpọ 'me duele la cabeza' tụọnụ na 'I hurt my head'. Ma 'hurt' tụọnụ na verb transitive na-eme ka ọ bụ na-eme ihe (ana m were isi m). Iji kwuo na ogologo, anyị na-eme ka ndị ahu na-akpọ 'have a headache' ma ọ bụ 'my head hurts'. Cheta: 'hurt' tụọnụ na verb intransitive (na-eme ka ọ bụ na-eme ihe) na-eme na ụdị ogologo, ma tụọnụ na subjectụụ ndị ahu (my head hurts). Cheta ka ị na-eme ka ndị ahu na-akpọ 'have' + noun tụọnụ na medical conditions.

examples.original: I have a cold.
examples.translation: Ana m enweta cold.
examples.note: Na-akpọ 'have' + disease ma ọ bụ symptom. Ọ bụghị ihe mere ka ị na-eme 'I am cold' tụọnụ na ọ bụ na ọ bụ cold, ọ bụ na ọ bụ na-eme na ị na-eme na ị na-eme na ị.

examples.original: I have a cough and a runny nose.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ hæv ə kɒf ænd ə ˈrʌni noʊz/
examples.translation: Ana m enweta cough na runny nose.
examples.note: N'ihi na ndoro ndoro na-akpọ 'and' bụ ndoro ndoro, ọ bụ na-akpọ 'cough and runny nose'. Cheta na 'runny nose' bụ 'nose na-eme'.

examples.original: I feel dizzy.
examples.translation: Ana m enweta dizzy.
examples.note: 'Feel' + adjective tụọnụ na physical states. Na Spanish, anyị na-eme ka ndị ahu na-akpọ 'me siento', ma na English, ọ bụghị ihe mere ka 'I feel me'.

examples.original: Take this medicine twice a day.
examples.translation: Gụọ ugwu a nkeji abụọ n'ụbọchị.
examples.note: Verb 'take' na-akpọ tụọnụ na medicines, ma ọ bụghị 'drink' (ime). 'Twice a day' bụ 'nkeji abụọ n'ụbọchị'.

examples.original: You should rest in bed.
examples.translation: Ị ga-eme ka ị nwere ike inye ugwo ugwu ugwu ugwu ugwu ugwu ugwu ugwu ugwu ugwu ugwu.
examples.note: Iji nyere ndoro ndoro, 'should' + infinitive verb. Ọ bụghị ihe mere ka 'must' (ndoro ndoro).

examples.original: I need to make an appointment.
examples.translation: Ana m enweta make an appointment.
examples.note: Na-akpọ 'make an appointment' tụọnụ na iji nyere ndoro ndoro. 'Need to' + verb na-eme ka ọ bụ na-eme na ndoro ndoro.

examples.original: My back hurts a lot.
examples.translation: Isi m na-eme nwayọ nwayọ nwayọ nwayọ nwayọ.
examples.note: 'A lot' n'okpuru ma ọ bụ n'oge verb. Ọ bụghị ihe mere ka 'my back hurts much' tụọnụ na 'a'.

examples.original: I have a sharp pain in my chest.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ hæv ə ʃɑːrp peɪn ɪn maɪ tʃɛst/
examples.translation: Ana m enweta sharp pain n'ime akwa m.
examples.note: Na-akpọ 'sharp' tụọnụ na sharp pain na 'dull' tụọnụ na dull pain. Cheta ka ị na-eme ka ndị ahu na-akpọ 'in my + ndị ahu' tụọnụ na location.

examples.original: My knee is swollen and red.
examples.translation: Akwa m na-eme swollen na red.
examples.note: Na-akpọ 'is' + adjective tụọnụ na state. Cheta na 'swollen' bụ adjective irregular.

title: Booking Accommodation / Nwere ajụjụ ọrịa
bridge: Na Spanish, anyị na-eme ka okwu 'reservar' dị mfe ('m reserve a room'), mana na English, ọtụtụ mmadụ na-eme ka okwu 'would like' + 'to book' iji zere ndoro. N'okpuru, ọ dị mkpa ịnweta ụzọ asụsụ na-egosi na okwu 'double room' na-adịbeghị n'okpuru nke ahu, mana na English, okwu ahu na-egosi n'elu nke ahu ('double room'). N'okpuru, na English, anyị na-eme ka okwu 'for' si n'ihi na ụbọchị ('for two nights'), mgbe na Spanish, anyị na-eme ka okwu 'por dos noches'.
rule: Iji reserve ọrịa na English na A2 level, biko, jiri okwu dịka: 'I would like to book...' (A chọrọ m ịbanye...), 'I'd like to make a reservation' (A chọrọ m ịme reservation). ịnwere ike ịbanye okwu dị iche iche na present simple iji mee ka ndoro dị: 'My name is...'. Na usoro ụbọchị, biko, jiri 'on' na-egosi ụbọchị ('on Monday') ma 'for' na-egosi ụbọchị ('for three nights'). Iji jụọ ihe ndoro dị, biko, jiri 'Do you have...?' ma 'Is there...?'. Ndoro ndoro dị iche: 'single room' (ndoro na-akpata ụmụnne), 'double room' (ndoro na-akpata ụmụnne abụọ), 'twin room' (ndoro na-akpata ụmụnne abụọ). Jiri n'okpuru, okwu ahu na-egosi n'elu nke ahu. Iji mee ka ndoro dị, biko, jiri 'with' (na-egosi na ọ dị): 'with a view' (na-egosi na ọ dị), 'with breakfast' (na-egosi na ọ dị breakfast).

concept_examples.text: I would like to book a double room for two nights.
concept_examples.translation: A chọrọ m ịbanye ndoro abụọ na-akpata ụmụnne abụọ na-akpata ụmụnne abụọ.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd laɪk tə bʊk ə ˈdʌbəl ruːm fɔː tuː naɪts/

concept_examples.text: Do you have any rooms available for this weekend?
concept_examples.translation: Ọ dị ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro?
concept_examples.phonetic: /duː juː hæv ˈɛni ruːmz əˈveɪləbəl fɔː ðɪs ˌwiːkˈɛnd/

concept_examples.text: I'd like a room with a sea view, please.
concept_examples.translation: A chọrọ m ndoro na-egosi na ụzọ anwụ, biko.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪd laɪk ə ruːm wɪð ə siː vjuː pliːz/

concept_examples.text: How much does it cost per night?
concept_examples.translation: Ọ bụ otu a na-egosi na ụbọchị?
concept_examples.phonetic: /haʊ mʌtʃ dʌz ɪt kɒst pɜː naɪt/

common_error.wrong: I want reserve a room for two nights.
common_error.correct: I would like to reserve a room for two nights.
common_error.correct_alt: I'd like to book a room for two nights.
common_error.explanation: Na Spanish, anyị na-eme ka okwu 'quiero reservar' na okwu 'querer', mana na English, 'want' bụ okwu dị mfe ma ọ bụrụ na ndoro ndoro. Ọ dị mkpa ịbanye 'would like' (a chọrọ m) iji zere ndoro. N'okpuru, na English, na-eme ka 'would like' si n'ihi na infinitive verb: 'I would like to reserve'. Mma ịbanye 'I want reserve' (n'ọnụ 'to'). ịnwere ike ịbanye 'book' (reserve) n'okpuru ndoro.

examples.original: Do you have a single room available?
examples.phonetic: /duː juː hæv ə ˈsɪŋɡəl ruːm əˈveɪləbəl/
examples.translation: Ọ dị ndoro na-akpata ụmụnne abụọ ndoro?
examples.note: Jiri 'Do you have...?' iji jụọ na present tense. 'Available' na-egosi n'okpuru nke ahu.

examples.original: Is there a room for tonight?
examples.translation: Ọ dị ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro?
examples.note: Jiri 'Is there...?' iji jụọ ihe ndoro dị.

examples.original: Are there any free rooms on Friday?
examples.phonetic: /ɑːr ðeər ˈɛni friː ruːmz ɒn ˈfraɪdeɪ/
examples.translation: Ọ dị ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro?
examples.note: Na plurals, jiri 'Are there any...?'. Jiri 'on' na-egosi ụbọchị.

examples.original: I'm sorry, we're fully booked.
examples.translation: Ọ dịghị m, anyị na-akpata ndoro ndoro.
examples.note: Okwu dị iche iji kwuo na ọ dịghị ndoro. 'Fully booked' na-egosi na ndoro dị mma.

examples.original: I'd like to book a double room for three nights.
examples.phonetic: /aɪd laɪk tə bʊk ə ˈdʌbəl ruːm fɔː θriː naɪts/
examples.translation: A chọrọ m ịbanye ndoro abụọ na-akpata ụmụnne abụọ na-akpata ụmụnne abụọ.
examples.note: Jiri 'I'd like' (na-egosi na 'would like') iji zere ndoro ma ọ bụrụ na ndoro.

examples.original: Can I reserve a room with a balcony?
examples.phonetic: /kæn aɪ rɪˈzɜːv ə ruːm wɪð ə ˈbælkəni/
examples.translation: Ọ dị m ịbanye ndoro na-egosi na ụzọ ndoro ndoro?
examples.note: Jiri 'Can I...?' iji jụọ ndoro. 'With' na-egosi na ọ dị.

examples.original: My name is Ana García. I have a reservation.
examples.phonetic: /maɪ neɪm ɪz ˈɑːnə ɡɑːrˈsiːə aɪ hæv ə ˌrezəˈveɪʃən/
examples.translation: Ahu m bụ Ana García. M na-akpata ndoro.
examples.note: Na mbata na hotel, jiri ahu gị ma ọ bụ na-akpata ndoro. 'Reservation' na-egosi na ndoro dị.

examples.original: I need to cancel my reservation.
examples.translation: A chọrọ m ịgụọ ndoro m.
examples.note: Jiri 'need to' + verb iji kwuo na ọ dị mkpa. 'Cancel' na-egosi na ọ dị.

levels.label: Questions about price and amenities
levels.translation: Jụọ ihe ndoro dị na ndoro

examples.original: How much is it per night?
examples.translation: Ọ bụ otu a na-egosi na ụbọchị?
examples.note: Jiri 'How much' iji jụọ ihe ndoro. 'Per night' na-egosi na 'na ụbọchị'.

examples.original: Does the price include breakfast?
examples.translation: Ọ dị ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro?
examples.note: Na third person singular, anyị na-eme ka 'Does' na-egosi na ọ dị. 'Include' na-egosi na 'ịnweta'.

examples.original: Is Wi-Fi free?
examples.translation: Ọ dị Wi-Fi na-egosi na ọ dị?
examples.note: Na English, 'is' na-egosi n'elu subject na-egosi na ọ dị. 'Free' na-egosi na 'na-egosi' ma ọ bụ 'na-egosi'.

examples.original: What time is check-out?
examples.translation: Ọ bụ otu a na-egosi na ụbọchị?
examples.note: 'Check-out' na-egosi na ụbọchị na-egosi na ọ dị, 'check-in' na-egosi na ụbọchị na-egosi na ọ dị. Ha na-egosi na okwu.

title: At the Bank or Exchange Office / Na ugwo na ego n'ulo ego ma obu na-egosi ego n'ulo ego
bridge: Na Igbo, mgbakwunye na okwu dị ka 'I would like...' maobu 'Can I...?' na-egosi okwu ndoro ndoro, mgbe na-esote nke Spanish na-egosi okwu dị ka 'Quisiera...' maobu '¿Me da...?'. N'ihi na na Igbo, okwu ndoro ndoro 'can' na 'would' na-akwado na okwu ndoro ndoro na-egosi okwu nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke. Na Igbo, nkeji nke ego na nkeji nke ego na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke. Na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke
rule: Iji mee ugwo maobu ihe na-egosi ego n'ulo ego maobu n'ulo ego, i ga-emepụta okwu ndoro ndoro na-egosi 'I would like' (m ga-emepụta) maobu na-egosi 'to' + okwu na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke. N'ihi na na Igbo, okwu ndoro ndoro 'can' na 'would' na-akwado na okwu ndoro ndoro na-egosi okwu nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke. Na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke. Na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke

concept_examples.text: I would like to exchange some dollars.
concept_examples.translation: A ga-emepụta ịgbanwe ego ndoro ndoro.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd laɪk tuː ɪksˈtʃeɪndʒ sʌm ˈdɑːlərz/

concept_examples.translation: Gịnị bụ nkeji nke ego n'egosi?

concept_examples.text: Can I open a bank account?
I need to withdraw some money.
concept_examples.translation: A chọrọ ịgwọta ego ndoro ndoro.

common_error.correct_alt: I would like to change money.
common_error.explanation: Na Spanish, anyị na-egosi 'quiero cambiar dinero' n'ọnụ ọgụgụ, mana na Igbo, okwu dị ka 'want' na 'would like' na-egosi okwu ndoro ndoro na-egosi 'to' n'elu okwu na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke. N'ihi na, i ga-emepụta 'I want to change...' maobu 'I would like to change...'. Okwu ndoro ndoro dị iche nke na-egosi 'want' na-egosi 'to' n'elu okwu na-egosi nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke.

levels.label: Basic Phrases for Exchanging Money
levels.translation: Okwu ndoro ndoro maka ịgbanwe ego

examples.original: I would like to exchange euros for pounds.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd laɪk tuː ɪksˈtʃeɪndʒ ˈjʊərəʊz fɔː paʊndz/
examples.translation: A ga-emepụta ịgbanwe euro n'ụra na pounds.
examples.note: Sịrị 'for' iji kwuo nkeji nke ego i chọrọ ịbanye.

examples.original: What is the rate for dollars?
examples.translation: Gịnị bụ nkeji nke ego n'egosi na dollars?
examples.note: Jụọ nkeji nke ego na-egosi 'rate'.

examples.original: Can I have some small bills?
examples.translation: Ọ ga-enyere m ego ndoro ndoro?
examples.note: 'Small bills' na-egosi ego nke na-egosi nke na-egosi nke.

examples.original: Is there a commission?
examples.translation: Ọ dị mma?
examples.note: Na Igbo, jụọ na-egosi 'Is there...?' maka okwu ndoro ndoro.

examples.original: I want to deposit this check into my account.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɒnt tuː dɪˈpɒzɪt ðɪs tʃek ˈɪntuː maɪ əˈkaʊnt/
examples.translation: A chọrọ m ịmepụta cheque a na akwụkwọ ego m.
examples.note: Sịrị 'into my account' iji kwuo ebe ego ga-abịa.

examples.original: Can you withdraw money from my account?
examples.phonetic: /kæn juː wɪðˈdrɔː ˈmʌni frɒm maɪ əˈkaʊnt/
examples.translation: Ọ ga-enyere m ịgwọta ego na akwụkwọ ego m?
examples.note: 'Withdraw from' bụ nkeji nke okwu ndoro ndoro.

examples.original: How much is the service fee?
examples.translation: Ego ndoro ndoro bụ nkeji nke ugwo?
examples.note: Jụọ nkeji nke ugwo na-egosi 'How much'.

examples.original: My account number is 12345.
examples.phonetic: /maɪ əˈkaʊnt ˈnʌmbər ɪz wʌn tuː θriː fɔː faɪv/
examples.translation: Nọmba akwụkwọ ego m bụ 12345.
examples.note: Na Igbo, nọmba na-egosi nọmba nọmba nọmba nọmba nọmba.

examples.original: I need to transfer money online.
examples.translation: A chọrọ m ịtụgharị ego na-egosi n'ime ugwo.
examples.note: Sịrị 'online' iji kwuo ugwo na-egosi n'ime ugwo.

examples.original: This is a currency exchange form.
examples.translation: A na-egosi ugwo nke nkeji nke ego n'ụwa.
examples.note: 'Currency' na-egosi nkeji nke ego n'ụwa.

translations.ig: Na ugwo na ego n'ulo ego maobu na-egosi ego n'ulo ego
